text:
maya: Heads-up — Product wants to trim the inference caching scope to hit the Q2 launch. They want to disable background cache priming for the hosted API to save ~2w of dev time. Do we accept or push back on SLOs?
lorenzo: Oof. Background priming reduces cold-cache p99 a lot. If we drop it we'll likely see cold-start p99 spikes on bigger prompt sets. Our target SLO is p99 < 250ms for interactive routes — this could push some customers over.
priyanka: Can we quantify? Quick rough RICE-ish: Reach: 700k requests/month for affected routes, Impact: medium (3), Confidence: 60, Effort saved: 2 dev-weeks -> RICE = (700k * 3 * 0.6) / 2 ? that's not normalized but gives sense. We should translate to product value vs reliability cost.
alex: Compromise proposal: keep priming for paid tiers / Dedicated + Private, remove for free/self-serve initially. Then run a 10% canary for hosted. If canary shows p99 impact < 10% we roll. Also add an automated fallback to re-enable priming for customers hitting p99 degradation.
jess: Operational note: current priming job is low-toil but does require a nightly sweep (~4h of runner time) and a few ad-hoc fixes every sprint. Removing it reduces immediate toil but increases incident risk. Toil burn-down shouldn't trade reliability for short-term developer time.
oncall-bot: incident:staging-cache-surge — last week we saw a 30% increase in cold-cache p99 during a staged rollout at 03:20 UTC. No customer-facing errors but latency jitter hit the alert threshold.
lorenzo: That incident is exactly why I'm cautious. The jitter didn't surface as errors but increased tail latency for some customers. If Product is OK with a higher initial tail, fine, but we should document launch criteria: canary pass, rollback plan, and SLO regression tolerance (e.g., no >5% relative p99 regression over 24h).
priyanka: Suggest we use a small spike instead of full removal: make priming async with lower priority, reduce frequency, and instrument cache-hit ratio per-customer. That reduces runner cost and gives data.
maya: Good tradeoffs. Product wants the ship date. We can do Alex's canary + Pr's async spike and set launch criteria: canary 10% for 72h, p99 regression <= 5% and no increase in error rate. If fail, revert and schedule dedicated backlog item.
alex: I'll draft the rollout playbook: steps, metrics (p50/p95/p99, cache-hit ratio, request volume), alert thresholds, and fast rollback command. Example rollback: `POST /admin/feature-flags/caching?state=on&scope=hosted` — keep admin hooks ready.
jess: Also add a short-term mitigation item: raise cache TTL for hot keys and enable per-customer priming flag so we can opt-in heavy customers. Low-effort and buys time.
priyanka: For prioritization board, I'll add a RICE card with normalized Reach (0.6), Impact (3), Confidence (0.6), Effort (2) => score ~0.54 normalized. Mark it as "defer if canary fails".
maya: Agreed. Action items: Alex: playbook + canary runbook, Pr: add RICE card on roadmap, Lorenzo/Jess: define rollback and mitigation knobs, I'll update PRD and ping Product to confirm the scope compromise. Happy to take ownership of the post-launch backlog if needed. :thumbsup:
lorenzo: Thanks. If canary passes we keep disabled priming for free-tier only and we re-evaluate after 1 sprint of telemetry.
maya: Closing loop — will update thread with the canary start time and the PRD link.
